| 🪢 Tangle · [q-0037.0013.0006](docs/questions/q-0037.0013.0006-how-is-the-path-ahead-found-and-shown-the-space-of-open-questions-and-tickets-mapped-from-the-roots-the-next-slices-ranked-by-a-stated-criterion-and-the-picture.md) · [q-0037.0012.0009](docs/questions/q-0037.0012.0009-how-is-an-amendment-to-an-instruction-tested-before-it-lands-against-which-cases-chosen-how-run-with-no-instruction-the-standing-one-and-the-new-one.md) · — · — |
|---|

| 📍 **q-0037.0013.0006** · How is the path ahead found and shown: the space of open questions and tickets mapped from the roots, the next slices ranked by a stated criterion, and the picture the person sees? |
|---|

Yes, and this conversation is the specimen. It began abstract, the pathfinder; derived a method, pacer and driver and weights; and the method bored back into the abstraction: the pacer dissolved, and the question I opened under it no longer fits its wording or its home.

The tree already holds the moves of that process, only never seen as one:

- **Down.** The general rule on a shape's structure asks the exact question: *does expanding its structure change the contract or even what the shape is?* (💡 [*The shape's structure*](AGENTS.md:22)). And the straw dog binds method text to the open abstraction whose answer will rewrite it, so the dependency is recorded at the moment it is created.
- **Up.** A missing parent is opened when a message is contained by none of the questions that resemble it. A question is reworded once the work shows its wording outdated, [q-0037.0001.0021](docs/questions/q-0037.0001.0021-how-is-a-question-reworded-once-the-work-shows-its-wording-is-outdated-and-when-does-rewording-replace-opening-a-parent.md). And how a change in one answer reaches what stood on it is [q-0037.0001.0023](docs/questions/q-0037.0001.0023-how-does-a-change-in-one-answer-reach-what-stood-on-it.md), unfolded into six parts and unanswered, which is the backtrack's hardest half.
- **The turn.** The pacer page's step-end choice, continue, repeat, decompose, *return upstream*, switch, ask. *Return upstream* is the backtrack itself, and it is the one move with no home: it sits in a document no instruction reads.

So I would build nothing for it. The backtrack is the driver's step-end rule with *return upstream* landed, recorded as the store's moves, open a parent, reword, re-parent, bind a straw dog, and the pathfinder's standing job is to redraw the path after each move (💡 [*Occam*](AGENTS.md:30)). What you perceive as a separate meta-process is the sequence of those moves seen whole. That whole is a picture the pathfinder can draw, the trail of a guess from abstraction to method and back, and a picture is the right form for it, not a mechanism.

One thing I will not claim: that recording the moves makes the backtrack cheap. Four drafts of q-0037.0001.0023 were reshaped before it unfolded, and it still has no answer. The moves are known; the judgment of when to return upstream is not, and that is what the driver's judges would have to carry.

The question's body now holds four passes, uncommitted. The next concrete step, if you take the shape, is the same as before: reword and move this question, open the driver's, and let the pathfinder's align begin with a discovery.

| ⚖️ Decisions |
|---|
| The split: pathfinder, driver, the ring's rules with *return upstream* landed, the pacer's name retired |
| Reword and move this question out from under the pacer, and open the driver's beside it |
| Commit the question's body as it stands |
| [q-0037.0012.0003](docs/questions/q-0037.0012.0003-what-does-an-entry-contract-version-cover.md) waits at `/align`, as the queue has held since 2026-10-08 |
